- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 90+ → 85–87), then correct downward — model fails to capture mean reversion after peaks.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day forecast, especially when true values are trending lower.
- Forecast lags behind true values by 1–3 days in the middle of the horizon (e.g., day 10–15), suggesting delayed reaction to new data.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward trends in the final 10 days, particularly when true values drop below 85.
- Model overreacts to recent high prices, producing overly optimistic forecasts when prices are near or above 90.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or cyclical patterns — e.g., consistent underestimation of 80–82 range when true values are 80–83.
- Model shows strong bias toward higher values in the first 5 days of forecast, then gradually corrects — suggesting a “warm-up” or “initial overconfidence” effect.
